        [1_000, "one K"],
        SEPARATING_LINE,

            "|    1000 | one K |",

The fix is complete and all tests pass.

## Summary

**Root cause:** In `_format_table` (tabulate/__init__.py:2369), every row — including `SEPARATING_LINE` rows — was passed through `pad_row`. Since `SEPARATING_LINE` is the string `"\001"`, `_pad_row` iterated it character-by-character, turning `"\001"` into `[" \001 "]` whenever `padding > 0`. The later `_is_separating_line([" \001 "])` check then returned `False` (because `" \001 " != "\001"`), so the row fell through to be rendered as an ordinary data row.

This is why formats with `padding=0` (like `simple`/`plain`) worked, but padded formats like `psql` (`padding=1`) rendered the line as `| |` instead of `|---------+-------|`. Mixing column types (numbers with strings) was just one trigger that exercises padded column widths.

**Fix:** Skip padding for separating-line rows so the marker stays intact and remains detectable:

```python
padded_rows = [
    row if _is_separating_line(row) else pad_row(row, pad) for row in rows
]
```

**Verification:** `python3 -m pytest test/ -q` now reports `257 passed, 20 skipped` (was `1 failed`), and the separating line renders as a horizontal rule across all `linebetweenrows=None` formats (psql, simple, plain, github, orgtbl, presto, rst, pipe) regardless of column-type mixing.
